questions.problem:
Find the solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{2}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 4 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}12 & -6 \\ -6 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}14 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the matrix on the left-hand side is invertible, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & ={[\begin{aligned}12 & -6 \\ -6 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}14 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12\cdot 5-(-6)\cdot (-6)}[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ 6 & 12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}14 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{24}[\begin{aligned}40 \\ 24\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3} \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & -27 \\ -27 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}c \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{2}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {1}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & -3 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 6 & -2 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & -3 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & -3 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}12 & -4 \\ 6 & -2 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & -3 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}81 & -27 \\ -27 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}12 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=81+9+12=102.
$$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 4 & 4 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}14 & 9 \\ 9 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the matrix on the left-hand side is invertible, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & ={[\begin{aligned}14 & 9 \\ 9 & 9\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{14\cdot 9-9\cdot 9}[\begin{aligned}9 & -9 \\ -9 & 14\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{45}[\begin{aligned}45 \\ -45\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
